\section{Related Work}

\paragraph{Execution Traces for Code LLMs.}
TracePile \citep{chen2025tracepile} scaled trace-augmented training to 2.6M samples; \citet{wang2025dcsh} found trace utility task- and format-dependent, which we extend by identifying exception events as the dominant signal.
NExT \citep{ni2024next} and ET-CoT \citep{eguchi2025etcot} used trace chain-of-thought for repair and execution reasoning; \citet{ferrando2025execute} found compact traces comparable to full traces, supporting our density finding.
\citet{liu2023codeexecution} pre-trained on execution traces; CRUXEval \citep{gu2024cruxeval,xu2025cruxevalx} established execution reasoning benchmarks.
None decompose which trace components contribute to \emph{classification} accuracy.

\paragraph{Code Verdict and Patch Classification.}
TRACED \citep{ding2024traced} showed execution-aware pretraining improves vulnerability detection; CC2Vec \citep{hoang2020cc2vec}, LLM4PatchCorrect \citep{zhou2024llm4patch}, and APPT \citep{appt2024} developed representation learning of code changes.
Verdict prediction is an instance of the test oracle problem \citep{barr2015oracle}; none isolate individual trace components.

\paragraph{Fault Localization and Trace Selection.}
SBFL \citep{abreu2007accuracy,jones2002visualization,wong2014dstar} and LLM-based FL \citep{kang2024autofl,qin2024agentfl} share our insight that anomalous execution events carry the strongest diagnostic signal.
TraceCoder \citep{huang2026tracecoder} and InspectCoder \citep{wang2025inspectcoder} use selective trace extraction; RepairAgent \citep{bouzenia2025repairagent}, Agentless \citep{xia2024agentless}, SWE-agent \citep{yang2024sweagent}, and OpenHands \citep{wang2025openhands} incorporate execution feedback in repair workflows \citep{jimenez2024swebench}, yet which trace components carry verdict signals most efficiently remains unstudied.
Prompt compression \citep{jiang2023llmlingua,li2023selectivecontext} showed pruning low-information tokens preserves accuracy; our decomposition quantifies \emph{why}.

\paragraph{Calibration, Data Selection, and Defect Prediction.}
Neural network calibration \citep{guo2017calibration}, extended to LLMs \citep{kadavath2022language,geng2024calibration,spiess2025calibration}, studies confidence-correctness alignment; our ECE ${<}$ 0.005 suggests compact inputs improve calibration.
Curriculum learning \citep{bengio2009curriculum}, dataset cartography \citep{swayamdipta2020cartography}, data selection \citep{sachdeva2024dataefficient,xie2023doremi}, and data pruning \citep{paul2021deep,sorscher2022beyond} show that removing low-value examples improves convergence, consistent with our finding that compact exceptions converge rapidly while verbose traces oscillate.
Just-in-time defect prediction \citep{kamei2013large} shares our fault detection motivation.

\paragraph{Connection to feature selection theory.}
Our findings provide empirical evidence that the classical principle of irrelevant features degrading classifier performance \citep{guyon2003introduction} manifests in SFT on execution traces.
The Information Bottleneck framework \citep{tishby2000information} predicts that optimal representations compress away task-irrelevant information; complete traces violate this by preserving all execution state.
LIMA \citep{zhou2023lima} shows that a small number of high-quality examples suffices for alignment, paralleling our finding that minimal diagnostic signals outperform verbose traces.

\paragraph{The marginal value of complete traces.}
Source code alone achieves 73--76\% across four models (\texttt{no\_trace}), so the total incremental value of traces is at most ${\sim}$27pp.
Complete traces capture only 4--9pp of this headroom (77--82\%), while exception events capture 24--27pp (${\geq}$99.33\%).
The finding that more information degrades performance, rather than the success of compact signals, is the primary contribution: it challenges the common assumption that richer execution context benefits SFT.

38	Source code alone achieves 73--76\% across four models (\texttt{no\_trace}), so the total incremental value of traces is at most ${\sim}$27pp.
39	Complete traces capture only 4--9pp of this headroom (77--82\%), while exception events capture 24--27pp (${\geq}$99.33\%).
40	The finding that more information degrades performance, rather than the success of compact signals, is the primary contribution: it challenges the common assumption that richer execution context benefits SFT.
41	This aligns with the classical principle that irrelevant features degrade classifiers \citep{guyon2003introduction}, the Information Bottleneck prediction that optimal representations compress task-irrelevant information \citep{tishby2000information}, and LIMA's \citep{zhou2023lima} demonstration that minimal high-quality data suffices for alignment.
42	
43	\paragraph{Design implications.}
44	The two-tier hierarchy (Table~\ref{tab:cross_model}) suggests a practical fallback: extract exception events first (explicit pathway); resort to tail-truncated execution state when no exception is raised (implicit pathway).
45	Tier~2 benefit is model-dependent (Qwen +10.9/+7.2pp at 7B/1.5B; CodeLlama +0.9pp), so trace design should match deployment model capacity.
46	Whether this framework transfers to other trace-based tasks \citep{gu2024cruxeval,ni2024next} remains open.

Source code alone achieves 73--76\% across four models (\texttt{no\_trace}), so the total incremental value of traces is at most ${\sim}$27pp.
Complete traces capture only 4--9pp of this headroom (77--82\%), while exception events capture 24--27pp (${\geq}$99.33\%).
The finding that more information degrades performance, rather than the success of compact signals, is the primary contribution: it challenges the common assumption that richer execution context benefits SFT.
This aligns with the classical principle that irrelevant features degrade classifiers \citep{guyon2003introduction}, the Information Bottleneck prediction that optimal representations compress task-irrelevant information \citep{tishby2000information}, and LIMA's \citep{zhou2023lima} demonstration that minimal high-quality data suffices for alignment.

\paragraph{Design implications.}
The two-tier hierarchy (Table~\ref{tab:cross_model}) suggests a practical fallback: extract exception events first (explicit pathway); resort to tail-truncated execution state when no exception is raised (implicit pathway).
Tier~2 benefit is model-dependent (Qwen +10.9/+7.2pp at 7B/1.5B; CodeLlama +0.9pp), so trace design should match deployment model capacity.
Whether this framework transfers to other trace-based tasks \citep{gu2024cruxeval,ni2024next} remains open.

\section{Related Work}

\paragraph{Execution Traces for Code LLMs.}
TracePile \citep{chen2025tracepile} scaled trace-augmented training to 2.6M samples; \citet{wang2025dcsh} found trace utility task- and format-dependent, which we extend by showing that complete traces degrade SFT performance while compact exception events suffice.
NExT \citep{ni2024next} and ET-CoT \citep{eguchi2025etcot} used trace chain-of-thought for repair and execution reasoning; \citet{ferrando2025execute} found compact traces comparable to full traces, supporting our density finding.
\citet{liu2023codeexecution} pre-trained on execution traces; CRUXEval \citep{gu2024cruxeval,xu2025cruxevalx} established execution reasoning benchmarks.
None decompose which trace components contribute to \emph{classification} accuracy.

\paragraph{Code Verdict and Patch Classification.}
TRACED \citep{ding2024traced} showed execution-aware pretraining improves vulnerability detection; CC2Vec \citep{hoang2020cc2vec}, LLM4PatchCorrect \citep{zhou2024llm4patch}, and APPT \citep{appt2024} developed representation learning of code changes.
Verdict prediction is an instance of the test oracle problem \citep{barr2015oracle}; none isolate individual trace components.

\paragraph{Fault Localization and Trace Selection.}
SBFL \citep{abreu2007accuracy,jones2002visualization,wong2014dstar} and LLM-based FL \citep{kang2024autofl,qin2024agentfl} share our insight that anomalous execution events carry the strongest diagnostic signal.
TraceCoder \citep{huang2026tracecoder} and InspectCoder \citep{wang2025inspectcoder} use selective trace extraction; RepairAgent \citep{bouzenia2025repairagent}, Agentless \citep{xia2024agentless}, SWE-agent \citep{yang2024sweagent}, and OpenHands \citep{wang2025openhands} incorporate execution feedback in repair workflows \citep{jimenez2024swebench}, yet which trace components carry verdict signals most efficiently remains unstudied.
Prompt compression \citep{jiang2023llmlingua,li2023selectivecontext} showed pruning low-information tokens preserves accuracy; our decomposition quantifies \emph{why}.

\paragraph{Calibration, Data Selection, and Defect Prediction.}
Neural network calibration \citep{guo2017calibration}, extended to LLMs \citep{kadavath2022language,geng2024calibration,spiess2025calibration}, studies confidence-correctness alignment; our ECE ${<}$ 0.005 suggests compact inputs improve calibration.
The Information Bottleneck \citep{tishby2000information} predicts optimal representations compress task-irrelevant information; feature selection theory \citep{guyon2003introduction} shows irrelevant features degrade classifiers; LIMA \citep{zhou2023lima} demonstrates minimal high-quality data suffices for alignment.
Curriculum learning \citep{bengio2009curriculum}, dataset cartography \citep{swayamdipta2020cartography}, data selection \citep{sachdeva2024dataefficient,xie2023doremi}, and data pruning \citep{paul2021deep,sorscher2022beyond} show that removing low-value examples improves convergence, consistent with our finding that compact exceptions converge rapidly while verbose traces oscillate.
Just-in-time defect prediction \citep{kamei2013large} shares our fault detection motivation.

Curriculum learning \citep{bengio2009curriculum}, dataset cartography \citep{swayamdipta2020cartography}, data selection \citep{sachdeva2024dataefficient,xie2023doremi}, and data pruning \citep{paul2021deep,sorscher2022beyond} show that removing low-value examples improves convergence, consistent with our finding that compact exceptions converge rapidly while verbose traces oscillate.
Just-in-time defect prediction \citep{kamei2013large} shares our fault detection motivation.

1	\section{Discussion}
2	\label{sec:discussion}
3	
4	\paragraph{A descriptive two-pathway framework.}
5	The results suggest execution traces contain two independent signal pathways for verdict prediction, whose interaction explains why complete traces degrade SFT learning.
6	We present this as a descriptive working hypothesis, not a causal model.
7	
8	\paragraph{Explicit pathway: diagnostic tokens.}
9	Exception and assertion events directly encode fault occurrence.
10	The diagnostic token ratio $d$ (\S2.1) correlates with accuracy at $r{=}0.949$ ($p{=}0.014$) across five conditions, and all four models achieve ${\geq}$99.33\% under \texttt{exception\_only} with zero variance on Qwen ($\sigma{=}$0.00, 3 seeds).
11	We acknowledge that exception events structurally encode verdict information; the contribution is systematic quantification across four models and three families.
12	Although 55.5\% of failures are silent logic errors, \texttt{exception\_only} achieves 100\% fail recall because test assertions generate \texttt{AssertionError} events, confirming the pathway captures both crashes and assertion failures.
13	\texttt{ae\_only}, a strict superset, slightly underperforms \texttt{exception\_only} (Table~\ref{tab:ablation}), confirming that additional content introduces noise.
14	
15	\paragraph{Implicit pathway: terminal execution state.}
16	Tail-truncated traces achieve 93--97\% accuracy (Table~\ref{tab:tail_cross_model}) despite containing near-zero diagnostic tokens ($d {\approx} 0$).
17	The mechanism: whole-input tail truncation at ${\geq}$512 tokens captures \texttt{[Line~X]} variable values at final execution steps, which indirectly encode program outcome.
18	Below 384 tokens, the globals module dump consumes the entire budget, yielding ${\sim}$73\% ($\approx$ \texttt{no\_trace}).
19	The +13.8pp phase transition at tail-384$\to$tail-512 marks where the model crosses this noise floor and accesses terminal execution state.
20	This pathway is genuinely non-obvious: it operates on structured program state with zero explicit fault markers.
21	
22	\paragraph{Diagnostic signal dilution in complete traces.}
23	Both pathways' signals exist in full traces but are buried under thousands of intermediate tokens.
24	Figure~\ref{fig:training_dynamics} confirms: \texttt{exception\_only} converges within 50 steps, while \texttt{full\_trace} with label-only loss oscillates (82--89\%) without convergence (Appendix~\ref{sec:training_dynamics}); seed variance negatively correlates with diagnostic density.
25	
26	\begin{figure}[t]
27	\centering
28	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{training_dynamics}
29	\caption{Training dynamics: \texttt{exception\_only} converges to 99.83\% by step 150; \texttt{full\_trace} with label-only loss oscillates (82--89\%) without convergence.}
30	\label{fig:training_dynamics}
31	\end{figure}
32	
33	\paragraph{Why SFT over regex?}
34	SFT \texttt{exception\_only} (99.83\%) exceeds the best regex (B\_marker, 99.33\%) by 0.50pp on 6 caught-exception boundary cases (McNemar $p{=}.014$), provides calibrated probabilities (ECE\,=\,0.0027; \S\ref{sec:calibration}), and retains 97.65\% under marker removal vs.\ B5's 28.49\% (\S\ref{sec:nomarker}).
35	The residual 2/1190 errors (both \texttt{GeneratorExit}; Appendix~\ref{sec:irreducible}) are shared across seeds; CodeLlama-13B seed 123 achieves 100\%.
36	
37	\paragraph{The marginal value of complete traces.}
38	Source code alone achieves 73--76\% across four models (\texttt{no\_trace}), so the total incremental value of traces is at most ${\sim}$27pp.
39	Complete traces capture only 4--9pp of this headroom (77--82\%), while exception events capture 24--27pp (${\geq}$99.33\%).
40	The finding that more information degrades performance, rather than the success of compact signals, is the primary contribution: it challenges the common assumption that richer execution context benefits SFT.
41	This aligns with the classical principle that irrelevant features degrade classifiers \citep{guyon2003introduction}, the Information Bottleneck prediction that optimal representations compress task-irrelevant information \citep{tishby2000information}, and LIMA's \citep{zhou2023lima} demonstration that minimal high-quality data suffices for alignment.
42	
43	\paragraph{Design implications.}
44	The two-tier hierarchy (Table~\ref{tab:cross_model}) suggests a practical fallback: extract exception events first (explicit pathway); resort to tail-truncated execution state when no exception is raised (implicit pathway).
45	Tier~2 benefit is model-dependent (Qwen +10.9/+7.2pp at 7B/1.5B; CodeLlama +0.9pp), so trace design should match deployment model capacity.
46	Whether this framework transfers to other trace-based tasks \citep{gu2024cruxeval,ni2024next} remains open.
47	
48	\paragraph{Caveats.}
49	The decomposition (\S\ref{sec:density}) is a preliminary upper-bound estimate on the Qwen family only (CodeLlama and DeepSeek exhibit label-only collapse); $N{=}4$ models is insufficient for a continuous density--accuracy relationship.
50	HumanEval/MBPP covers only simple assert-based tests; real-world failure modes remain untested.
51

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The Director issued a **Comprehensive Rewrite** instruction for the EMNLP 2026 paper (DDL 5/25, 3 days away). Round 15 reviewer gave Overall 3.0 (Findings level). The core reframe shifts from "exceptions help" to "complete traces hurt." Specific requirements:
   
   **Phase 1 (immediate, no new experiment data needed):**
   - Rewrite Abstract, Introduction, §3.4 Decomposition, Discussion, Conclusion, Limitations
   - New C1-C4 contribution structure emphasizing complete trace degradation
   - B5 regex promoted to primary baseline in Table 1 and §3.1
   - Nomarker ablation promoted to formal ablation
   - Decomposition downgraded: "confounded upper-bound estimate" language, explicit confounders listed
   - "information overload" → first occurrence in quotes, all subsequent → "diagnostic signal dilution"
   - "two-pathway model" → "two-pathway descriptive framework"
   - Add ML theory connections (Tishby, Guyon & Elisseeff, LIMA)
   - Add no_trace baseline discussion paragraph
   - SF-8: Add citations for Tishby 2000, Guyon 2003, Zhou 2023 LIMA, Paul 2021, Sorscher 2022
   - M-1: Anonymize GPU name
   - M-2: Delete orphan pornprasit2021jitline; verify qwen2025coder→qwen2024coder
   - M-3: First Table 1 reference mention dagger
   - M-5: Figure 2 → figure* (full-width); Figure 5 increase axis tick font
   - Must maintain ≤8 pages main body
   - Post-edit grep checks: "traceback"=0, "82.9"=0, "information overload"=1 (quoted), "gradient dilution eliminated"=0, "+11.0"=0

   **Phase 2 (deferred, awaiting experiment data):**
   - Cross-dataset complete results (MBPP→HE still RUNNING)
   - Holm-Bonferroni adjusted p-values
   - Problem-level clustered bootstrap CI
   - Oscillation metrics
   - k-means tier validation
   - SF-4 complete training dynamics figure

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Reframe direction**: "complete traces hurt" instead of "exceptions help"
   - **Two-pathway descriptive framework** (renamed from "model"): explicit (exception events) + implicit (terminal execution state via tail truncation)
   - **Diagnostic signal dilution** (replaces "information overload"): thousands of irrelevant trace tokens dilute diagnostic signals at inference
   - **Confounded upper-bound estimate**: label-only loss ablation simultaneously changes gradient selection (~1/500 tokens receive loss), implicit regularization (NTP removed), and effective learning rate
   - **B5 regex as primary baseline**: 99.33% via format marker, collapses to 28.49% on marker removal while SFT retains 97.65%
   - **Cross-dataset transfer**: HE→MBPP exception_only 99.41%, no_trace 70.56%
   - **Page budget management**: EMNLP 8-page main body limit with aggressive content additions requiring compression
   - **Globals module dump threshold**: ~384 tail tokens consumed by noise; structured [Line X] markers visible above ~512

3. Files and Code Sections:

   - **`/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_4/projects/trace-verdict-study/docs/paper/main.tex`**
     - Contains Abstract (rewritten) and Limitations (expanded)
     - Abstract rewrite: "barely improving over source code alone (~73-76%)", B5 regex + nomarker + cross-dataset, "diagnostic signal dilution", "confounded upper-bound estimate"
     - Limitations expanded from 3→5 points: assert-based tests, scale (30B+), 3-seed minimum, full_trace not on DebugBench, decomposition confounders with gradient masking future work
     - New Abstract:
       ```latex
       \begin{abstract}
       Complete execution traces contain all information needed for verdict prediction (classifying whether a test passes or fails), yet they actively impair SFT learning.
       Across four models spanning three architecture families (1.5B--13B parameters), complete traces achieve only 77--82\%, barely improving over source code alone (${\sim}$73--76\%) and trailing compact exception events (${\geq}$99.33\%) by 18+pp.
       A regex exploiting format markers matches the exception ceiling (99.33\%), but marker removal collapses it to 28.49\% while SFT retains 97.65\%; cross-dataset transfer (99.41\%) confirms SFT acquires genuine diagnostic pattern recognition beyond format matching.
       A preliminary decomposition (confounded upper-bound estimate on the Qwen family) attributes ${\geq}$74\% of the degradation to diagnostic signal dilution at inference, though the label-only ablation simultaneously alters gradient selection, regularization, and effective learning rate.
       A two-tier signal hierarchy holds across families, with a sharp performance transition at ${\sim}$512 tail tokens, yielding a practical trace selection strategy: extract exception events first (Tier~1, ${\geq}$98.53\%), fall back to tail-truncated state otherwise (93--97\%).
       For SFT-based verdict prediction, the binding constraint is diagnostic signal density, not information quantity.
       \end{abstract}
       ```
     - New Limitations:
       ```latex
       \section*{Limitations}
       Our study has several limitations.
       First, all experiments use HumanEval and MBPP-sanitized (591 problems, simple assert-based tests on short Python functions); generalization to human-written code, other languages, non-assert test frameworks (e.g., parametric tests, integration tests, flaky tests), and multi-file projects is unverified.
       Second, all four models (1.5B--13B) are code-specialized; models at 30B+ parameters may have sufficient capacity to overcome diagnostic signal dilution, and general-purpose LLMs may behave differently.
       Third, multi-seed experiments use only 3 seeds (the minimum for variance estimation); larger seed pools would strengthen robustness claims.
       Fourth, \texttt{full\_trace} was not evaluated on DebugBench due to the supplementary nature of that analysis; whether complete traces degrade on human-written buggy code remains untested.
       Fifth, the decomposition (\S\ref{sec:density}) is a confounded upper-bound estimate limited to the Qwen family; future work should isolate individual confounders through controlled gradient masking ablations.
       ```

   - **`introduction.tex`**
     - Fully rewritten by Worker. New framing: "complete traces hurt" not "exceptions help"
     - B5 regex introduced as PRIMARY baseline in para 4
     - Nomarker + cross-dataset evidence immediately following
     - "information overload" appears once in quotes (line 19): `diagnostic signal dilution (the mechanism underlying what is intuitively termed ``information overload'')`
     - New C1-C4 contributions:
       - C1: "Complete traces are strictly dominated by compact exception events"
       - C2: "SFT learns genuine diagnostic patterns beyond format matching"
       - C3: "A two-tier signal hierarchy with a practical trace selection strategy"
       - C4: "Preliminary decomposition of the full-trace degradation"

   - **`experiments.tex`**
     - §3.4 title: `\subsection{Preliminary Decomposition (Confounded Upper-Bound Estimate)}`
     - Table 3 caption updated: added specific confounders "(~1/500 tokens receive loss), implicit regularization (NTP on trace tokens removed), and effective learning rate"
     - B5 regex row added to Table 1: `Regex B5 (marker) & \multicolumn{4}{c}{99.33} \\`
     - Dagger + B5 context at first Table 1 reference: "single-seed entries are marked with $^\dag$. Regex B5 (99.33\%) exploits the \texttt{[No exception data in trace]} format marker..."
     - "information overload" → "diagnostic signal dilution" (3 instances at lines ~154, 156, 158)
     - Figure 2: Changed to figure* then REVERTED back to figure due to page overflow
     - Figure 2 remains single-column `\begin{figure}[t]` with `\columnwidth`

   - **`discussion.tex`**
     - Full rewrite with compressed content:
     - "A two-pathway model" → "A descriptive two-pathway framework" + "descriptive working hypothesis, not a causal model"
     - "Noise dilution" → "Diagnostic signal dilution in complete traces"
     - Explicit pathway compressed (removed "We acknowledge..." sentence)
     - Implicit pathway compressed (merged two sentences)
     - "Why SFT over regex?" compressed (removed residual error sentence)
     - NEW "The marginal value of complete traces" paragraph: no_trace 73-76%, traces add ≤27pp, complete traces capture only 4-9pp, ML theory connections (Guyon, Tishby, LIMA)
     - Design implications paragraph trimmed

   - **`conclusion.tex`**
     - Expanded from 3→5 sentences (compressed from initial 6):

\section{Related Work}

\paragraph{Execution Traces for Code LLMs.}
TracePile \citep{chen2025tracepile} scaled trace-augmented training to 2.6M samples; \citet{wang2025dcsh} found trace utility task- and format-dependent, which we extend by showing that complete traces degrade SFT performance while compact exception events suffice.
NExT \citep{ni2024next} and ET-CoT \citep{eguchi2025etcot} used trace chain-of-thought for repair and execution reasoning; \citet{ferrando2025execute} found compact traces comparable to full traces, supporting our density finding.
\citet{liu2023codeexecution} pre-trained on execution traces; CRUXEval \citep{gu2024cruxeval,xu2025cruxevalx} established execution reasoning benchmarks.
None decompose which trace components contribute to \emph{classification} accuracy.

\paragraph{Code Verdict and Patch Classification.}
TRACED \citep{ding2024traced} showed execution-aware pretraining improves vulnerability detection; CC2Vec \citep{hoang2020cc2vec}, LLM4PatchCorrect \citep{zhou2024llm4patch}, and APPT \citep{appt2024} developed representation learning of code changes.
Verdict prediction is an instance of the test oracle problem \citep{barr2015oracle}; none isolate individual trace components.

\paragraph{Fault Localization and Trace Selection.}
SBFL \citep{abreu2007accuracy,jones2002visualization,wong2014dstar} and LLM-based FL \citep{kang2024autofl,qin2024agentfl} share our insight that anomalous execution events carry the strongest diagnostic signal.
TraceCoder \citep{huang2026tracecoder} and InspectCoder \citep{wang2025inspectcoder} use selective trace extraction; RepairAgent \citep{bouzenia2025repairagent}, Agentless \citep{xia2024agentless}, SWE-agent \citep{yang2024sweagent}, and OpenHands \citep{wang2025openhands} incorporate execution feedback in repair workflows \citep{jimenez2024swebench}, yet which trace components carry verdict signals most efficiently remains unstudied.
Prompt compression \citep{jiang2023llmlingua,li2023selectivecontext} showed pruning low-information tokens preserves accuracy; our decomposition quantifies \emph{why}.

\paragraph{Calibration, Data Selection, and Defect Prediction.}
Neural network calibration \citep{guo2017calibration}, extended to LLMs \citep{kadavath2022language,geng2024calibration,spiess2025calibration}, studies confidence-correctness alignment; our ECE ${<}$ 0.005 suggests compact inputs improve calibration.
The Information Bottleneck \citep{tishby2000information}, feature selection theory \citep{guyon2003introduction}, and LIMA \citep{zhou2023lima} predict that compressing task-irrelevant information improves learning; data pruning \citep{paul2021deep,sorscher2022beyond} and curriculum learning \citep{bengio2009curriculum} confirm this empirically, consistent with our finding that compact exceptions converge rapidly while verbose traces oscillate.
Just-in-time defect prediction \citep{kamei2013large} shares our fault detection motivation.

\section{Conclusion}

Across four models (1.5B--13B, three families), complete execution traces (77--82\%) barely improve over source code alone (${\sim}$73--76\%) while compact exception events achieve ${\geq}$99.33\%; cross-dataset transfer (99.41\%) and marker-removal robustness (97.65\% vs.\ regex collapse to 28.49\%) confirm SFT learns genuine diagnostic patterns.
A two-tier signal hierarchy yields a practical trace selection strategy: extract exception events first, fall back to tail-truncated state (93--97\%) otherwise.
A preliminary decomposition attributes ${\geq}$74\% of the degradation to diagnostic signal dilution at inference (confounded upper-bound estimate); controlled gradient masking ablations remain the critical next step.
These findings suggest that trace-based tool design should prioritize diagnostic density over completeness.
Generalization to human-written code, other languages, non-assert tests, and larger models remains open.

\section{Introduction}

Execution traces (line-by-line records of a program's runtime behavior) have emerged as a promising input modality for code language models \citep{chen2025tracepile,ding2024traced,wang2025dcsh,ni2024next}.
The intuition is straightforward: more execution information should help the model make better predictions.
Yet for verdict prediction (classifying whether a test passes or fails), this intuition is wrong.
Complete traces \emph{actively degrade} accuracy compared to compact exception events, despite containing strictly more information.

Prior work found trace utility to be task-dependent \citep{wang2025dcsh}, but focused on generation-oriented tasks where output noise confounds the analysis.
Verdict prediction offers a cleaner testbed: as binary classification, it isolates the learning signal from generation noise, and controlled component ablation directly measures how trace content affects SFT learning.
This approach aligns with recent *CL precedent: CRUXEval \citep{gu2024cruxeval} uses execution prediction to probe code reasoning, and NExT \citep{ni2024next} uses trace-augmented chain-of-thought for program repair.

We present a systematic component ablation of trace representations for verdict prediction.
Using 591 problems from HumanEval \citep{chen2021evaluating} and MBPP-sanitized \citep{austin2021program}, we evaluate four models across three architecture families and 1.5B to 13B parameters: Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B/1.5B-Instruct \citep{qwen2024coder}, CodeLlama-13B-Instruct \citep{roziere2024code}, and DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B-Instruct \citep{deepseek2024coder}.

The central result: complete traces (77--82\%) barely improve over source code alone (${\sim}$73--76\%) while exception events achieve ${\geq}$99.33\% across all models and seeds (\S\ref{sec:cross_model}).
A simple regex baseline (B5) that exploits the \texttt{[No exception data in trace]} format marker matches this ceiling at 99.33\%; even a trivial pattern suffices, so the interesting question is not why exceptions help but \emph{why complete traces hurt}.
Marker removal collapses B5 to 28.49\% while SFT retains 97.65\% ($-$2.01pp); cross-dataset transfer at 99.41\% (HumanEval${\to}$MBPP) confirms that SFT acquires genuine diagnostic patterns beyond format matching (\S\ref{sec:nomarker}).

A preliminary decomposition on the Qwen family (7B and 1.5B, 3 seeds each) provides a confounded upper-bound estimate: gradient dilution accounts for ${\leq}$26\% of the gap, with diagnostic signal dilution (the mechanism underlying what is intuitively termed ``information overload'') at ${\geq}$74\%, though the label-only ablation simultaneously alters gradient selection, regularization, and effective learning rate (\S\ref{sec:density}).
Training dynamics confirm this: \texttt{exception\_only} converges within 50 steps, while \texttt{full\_trace} oscillates between 82--89\% without stable convergence (\S\ref{sec:ablation}, Appendix~\ref{sec:training_dynamics}).
A tail-truncation budget sweep reveals a sharp performance jump at ${\sim}$512 tokens; this threshold coincides with the globals module dump (${\sim}$384 tokens), beyond which structured \texttt{[Line~X]} variable values appear (\S\ref{sec:trace_length}).

Our contributions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Complete traces are strictly dominated by compact exception events}: across four models (1.5B--13B, three families), complete traces (77--82\%) barely improve over source code alone (${\sim}$73--76\%) while exception events achieve ${\geq}$99.33\% (\S\ref{sec:cross_model}). Training dynamics directly show the mechanism: \texttt{exception\_only} converges within 50 steps while \texttt{full\_trace} oscillates without stable convergence (\S\ref{sec:ablation}, Appendix~\ref{sec:training_dynamics}).

\item \textbf{SFT learns genuine diagnostic patterns beyond format matching}: a regex exploiting format markers matches the exception ceiling (99.33\%), but marker removal collapses it to 28.49\% while SFT retains 97.65\% ($-$2.01pp); cross-dataset transfer at 99.41\% confirms the learned signal generalizes (\S\ref{sec:nomarker}).

\item \textbf{A two-tier signal hierarchy with a practical trace selection strategy}: Tier~1 (exceptions, assertions; ${\geq}$98.53\%) dominates Tier~2 (loop compression; 77--86\%) by 12+pp with non-overlapping CIs across all four models. A sharp performance transition at ${\sim}$512 tail tokens yields a practical fallback: exception events first, tail-truncated state otherwise (\S\ref{sec:ablation}, \S\ref{sec:trace_length}).

\item \textbf{Preliminary decomposition of the full-trace degradation}: a confounded upper-bound estimate via label-only loss on the Qwen family (7B and 1.5B, 3 seeds each) attributes gradient dilution ${\leq}$26\% and diagnostic signal dilution ${\geq}$74\% of the gap, though the ablation simultaneously alters gradient selection, regularization, and effective learning rate (\S\ref{sec:density}).
\end{enumerate}
